risks: All 10 domains checked were taken, which shows heavy existing use (a web search was not run). German/Serbian 'takt' also means tact, which is harmless. English speakers may spell it 'tact' after hearing it. Included only as an exceptional story, since there is no domain.
why_cool: It is the hardest-sounding name here (K-T), one syllable, and has a genuine process-engineering hidden story that engineers recognize instantly.

name: Solidus
story: Expansion: S = Scope, O = Own, L = Learn, I = Iterate, D = Deliver, U = Users, S = Support. The word has a double hidden story. First, Constantine's gold coin (309 AD) stayed stable for about 700 years and gave English 'solid' and 'soldier'. Second, SOLIDUS is the official Unicode name of '/' (U+002F), the root of every file path, which fits the terminal/CLI motif.
risks: Heavy conflicts: Solidus is a well-known open-source Rails e-commerce framework (solidus.io), Solidus Systems is a web/app agency doing the same services, and there is also Solidus Technical Solutions, plus Solidus Labs (crypto surveillance) and the Metal Gear Solid character Solidus Snake. It is 7 letters and 3 syllables, the softest name in the set.
why_cool: The '/' easter egg is a builder-to-builder hidden story no other candidate has, combined with the gold-standard value meaning.

name: Remek
story: Hungarian 'remek' means masterpiece, and also splendid. In the Hungarian guild (céh) system the remek was the piece a journeyman had to make and submit to the guild masters before he could be admitted as a master; the German equivalent is Meisterstück. The word passed into Serbian and Croatian as 'remek-delo' / 'remek-djelo' (masterpiece), so it links Belgrade with Central European guild tradition. Tie to the brand: every product and every client build is treated as a remek, the work that proves mastery, judged by an owner's standards. It works as a quiet holding and as an umbrella ('Quicktalog by Remek', 'Remek Labs'). It fits with the Esnaf/Kalfa guild thread already in the lead's pool as the missing final step: apprentice, journeyman, masterpiece.
risks: Existing: Remek! Trading Systems (Toronto, small NinjaTrader algo-trading software vendor), Remek AS (Norway), Remek Group. A listener could think 'remake' or spell it 'Remeck'. It sounds a little like Rimac (Croatian hypercar maker). No negative meanings known in EN/SR/DE/ES/FR/IT/HU; in Hungarian it is positive ('splendid'). The .com, .co, .so and .ai are taken.
why_cool: Five letters, a hard -k close, open vowels, spelled as spoken. It sounds like a first name (Remek is a Polish diminutive of Remigiusz), and the masterpiece story is real and easy to find. Short and hard like Braze, with an old-guild weight like Adacta.

name: Farga
story: Catalan and Occitan 'farga' means forge or ironworks. The 'farga catalana' (Catalan forge) was a water-powered bloomery that turned ore straight into wrought iron in one furnace. It spread across the Pyrenees and to the Americas and was used into the 19th century. Tie to the brand: a place that turns raw material into high-value finished product, in the same loop as Scope -> Build -> Ship. It also nods to the founder's process-engineering background (a furnace as a single-step reactor).
risks: La Farga is a large Catalan copper and metals producer (industrial, not software), and 'Apoyo La Farga' is a school tutoring app. A listener might hear 'Fargo' (the film or city). The standard Spanish word is 'fragua', and 'farga' has no negative meaning known in ES/EN/SR/DE/IT/FR/HU. The .com, .studio, .so and .app are taken.
why_cool: A hard F with an -rg- core and open 'a' vowels, in the same family as Braze, Adacta and Koshava. Five letters, it sounds like a name, and it hides a real forge story. farga.co and farga.ai are both open, which is rare for a five-letter real word.

name: Tanren
story: Japanese 鍛錬 'tanren'. 鍛 (tan) means to forge or hammer metal, and 錬 (ren) means to refine or temper it. Together the word means forging and tempering, and figuratively disciplined training until mastery. In The Book of Five Rings, Miyamoto Musashi writes that a thousand days of practice is 'tan' (forging) and ten thousand days is 'ren' (refining). Tie to the brand: products are hammered into shape, then refined through iteration, which is the Build -> Ship & iterate loop, done by people who own the result.
risks: Existing uses: TANREN, a Japanese sales-enablement learning platform; TanRen Software Development S.A. (small); several open-source learning apps named Tanren on GitHub. It is softer than the founder's hard-onset favourites. The .com, .co, .so, .ai, .app and labs.com are all taken.
why_cool: Clean, two syllables, spelled exactly as heard, with a samurai-smith story under it. It reads like a founder's surname and passes the radio test easily. The metal meaning and the training meaning together match 'products plus services done with mastery'.

name: Mokume
story: Japanese 木目 'mokume' means wood grain, from mokume-gane (木目金, 'wood-grain metal'). This is a 17th-century technique credited to Denbei Shoami of Akita: layers of different metals (copper, silver, gold, shakudō) are fused into one billet, then carved and forged until a flowing grain appears. Tie to the brand: different disciplines (engineering, AI, data, design) are fused into one solid, beautiful product. It is a direct cousin of brazing (the founder's Braze anchor) and of his metallurgy and process-engineering background.
risks: Mokume Software Inc. (Redwood City data-management firm) was acquired by Versant around 2002 and is now defunct. Jewelers use 'mokume gane' heavily. It has three soft syllables with no hard close, and English speakers may say 'moke-yoom'. The .com, .co, .so and .app are taken.
why_cool: The hidden story fits the founder's Braze love exactly: joining metals into something more valuable than its parts. It is a real, discoverable craft with striking visuals for a brand (grain patterns), and it sounds like a name.

name: Ktema
story: Ancient Greek κτῆμα 'ktēma' means a possession: property, something acquired and kept. Thucydides (History 1.22) wrote that his work was composed as 'ktēma es aiei', 'a possession for all time', not a showpiece for a moment's applause. Tie to the brand: this is ownership stated outright. The company builds products it owns and work meant to last, not throwaway client deliverables. The name suits a holding and later an umbrella.
pronunciation: k'TAY-mah (3 syllables; the initial k is lightly sounded)
risks: The initial kt- cluster weakens the radio test: many English speakers will hear 'Tema' or 'Kuh-tema' and spell it wrong. In modern Greek κτήμα means estate or farm and appears in many winery names (usually romanised 'Ktima'). The .com and .so are taken.
why_cool: It has the strongest ownership story of the set, from one of the most quoted lines in Western history. The -kt- core matches the Adacta and Bract texture, it has old-root enterprise weight, and it has the widest open domain set in this territory.

name: Noren
story: Japanese 暖簾 'noren' is the split fabric curtain hung at a shop entrance, bearing the house crest. Over centuries it came to stand for the shop's reputation and goodwill, and 'noren' (のれん) is literally the Japanese accounting term for goodwill. 'Noren-wake' (dividing the noren) is the custom of a master letting a trusted apprentice open a new shop under the house name. Tie to the brand: this fits the quiet-holding-now, umbrella-later plan. Each product (Quicktalog, unbg, Shot & Share) hangs under the same noren, and the name itself means the value built by doing work well.
risks: It is soft, with no hard plosive, so it is off the founder's Br-/-ze profile. A listener might spell it 'Noreen' or 'Norén' (a Swedish surname). Many restaurants and shops use the name. Domain position is weak: only noren.build is open among those checked.
why_cool: The best umbrella story in the set: the name literally means brand equity, and there is an old custom for spinning off new ventures under it. It is short, sounds like a name, and has a quiet, serious feel.

name: Meijin
story: Japanese 名人 'meijin', literally 'famous person', means a master or virtuoso. It is the supreme title in Go and shogi, dating to the early 1600s; Honinbo Sansa is recognised as the first Go Meijin, in 1612. Kawabata's novel 'Meijin' (The Master of Go) chronicles the last retirement game of a Meijin. Tie to the brand: mastery that is earned and recognised by peers, a builder-to-builder title rather than a sales claim.
risks: The radio test is middling: a listener may spell it 'Mayjin' or 'Mejin'. Shanxi Meijin Energy is a large Chinese energy company, not tech, and a few small or dissolved UK consultancies used the name. There are anime and game title associations. The .co, .so and .app are taken.
why_cool: Short, with a crisp -j- core, and it sounds like a name. It has the strategy-game prestige that appeals to engineers, and meijin.studio and meijinlabs.com are both open.

name: Fabbro
story: Italian 'fabbro' means smith or craftsman (from Latin faber). In Purgatorio XXVI Dante calls the troubadour Arnaut Daniel 'il miglior fabbro del parlar materno', 'the better craftsman of the mother tongue'. T.S. Eliot then dedicated The Waste Land to Ezra Pound as 'il miglior fabbro'. Tie to the brand: 'the better maker' is a quiet, literary claim of mastery, owned by the people who do the work.
risks: It shares a root with 'Faber', which is already in the lead strategist's pool, so it may read as a variant rather than a new idea. A listener might spell it 'Fabro' (single b). It is a common Italian surname and trade word (e.g. plumbers' and locksmiths' signage in Italy). The .co and .studio are taken.
why_cool: A hard F and -bbr- core that echo Braze and Brame, with one of the best-known hidden stories in modern literature. It sounds like a surname, it is European and serious, and fabbrolabs.com is open.

name: Vasara
story: Finnish 'vasara' means hammer: the smith's tool, as in the Kalevala, where Ilmarinen forges the Sampo. In Lithuanian and Latvian 'vasara' means summer, which gives a warm second reading. Tie to the brand: the maker's primary tool, which shapes raw material into value, with a Nordic-Baltic old root.
risks: 'Vasara' is also Taito's arcade shoot-'em-up (2000), and the name recalls Japanese 'Basara'. Three syllables with a soft middle s, so it is less hard than the brief's profile. The .co, .so, .app and labs.com are taken.
why_cool: Open 'a' vowels in a row, like Koshava and Adacta, with a hidden hammer inside. Spelled as spoken, it sounds like a name, and it has a friendly international feel.

name: Varpet
story: Armenian վարպետ 'varpet' means master craftsman. It is also a national title of honour: in his last years the poet Avetik Isahakyan was called simply 'Varpet', the Master. Tie to the brand: a maker recognised as master by the people he builds for, which fits an ownership-minded studio.
risks: Real conflict: Varpet is an Armenian home-services marketplace app (varpet.com, varpet.us, 'Varpet Partner' app) that uses the same 'master' meaning. The '-pet' ending can read as cute and rhymes with 'carpet'. The .com is taken.
why_cool: A hard V-r-p consonant frame, six letters, and a genuine honorific story that few Western brands have. Both .co and .studio are open.

name: Zunft
story: German 'Zunft' means craft guild. The medieval Zünfte set quality standards, trained apprentices, examined masterpieces and certified masters. In Zurich the guilds still govern civic tradition and parade at Sechseläuten, when they burn the Böögg to call spring. Tie to the brand: a guild of builders who hold their own work to a master's standard, whether it is their product or a client's.
risks: It has two pronunciations (English z- vs German ts-), which hurts the radio test, and the -nft cluster is harsh. The root is German only and may feel bureaucratic. The .co, .com and .so are taken.
why_cool: One hard syllable with a Z onset, as short and blunt as Braze. The old European guild story gives enterprise gravity.

name: Arotz
story: Basque 'arotz' means craftsman: the artisan who works wood or iron (carpenter or smith, depending on dialect). Basque is Europe's oldest living language isolate, older than the Indo-European languages around it. Tie to the brand: the maker in the oldest living European tongue, a hidden story of craft that predates everything else.
risks: A listener might spell it 'Arots' or 'Arrotz'. 'Rots' is embedded (English 'rot'). It is an obscure root that needs explaining. The .com and .so are taken.
why_cool: A -tz close like Braze's -ze, short, and exotic but readable, with a very open domain position (.co, .studio and .app all available).

name: Vardar
story: The Vardar is the river that runs from North Macedonia to the Aegean, and it gives its name to the Vardarec (Greek: Vardaris), a cold, dry north wind that funnels down the valley to Thessaloniki. It is the Balkan sibling of the Koshava (Belgrade) and the Mistral (Rhône), which makes it the 'local natural phenomenon' option in the founder's Koshava style. Tie to the brand: a steady force channelled through a narrow valley, i.e. focus that becomes power.
risks: It is a river and region name with Macedonian political connotations (historical 'Vardar Macedonia', the Greece-Macedonia naming dispute), and several sports clubs use it (RK/FK Vardar). The story is about nature, not making or ownership. It may sound like 'Vader' or 'radar'. The .co is taken.
why_cool: Hard, symmetrical, radar-like sound. Six letters, spelled as spoken, and a real Balkan wind story that global audiences can say, like Koshava but easier.
